RagShortTexts: The Order of Santiago bore red sword-crosses, safeguarding the pilgrimage route to Compostela.

Variants.Content: Named for Saint James the Moor-slayer, the Order of Santiago carried red sword-cross emblems. Allowing married knights under Augustinian rule, it attracted the cream of Castilian and Leonese nobility, guarding both the pilgrim road to Compostela and frontline pastures in Extremadura.
The Grand Master commanded immense revenues across royal domains. Blending secular inheritance with knightly brotherhood, Santiago fielded disciplined divisions during royal Andalusian sieges.
Pilgrim hospices and bridges along the Camino are sustained by Santiago commanderies. When mountain brigands strike unwary travelers, knights ride out promptly to hang culprits along roadsides.
